name: Kawasaki KLR650
intro: The second-generation KLR. Simple, cheap and owner-maintained, with one famous weak part: the doohickey.

A-002.title: Check for open recalls
A-002.instructions: Run your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. 2008-2009 bikes had recalls for the muffler mount bolts (09V059) and a wiring harness that can chafe on the frame (09V062), and 2008 bikes for the turn signals (08V520).
A-002.reason: These were all fixed free by dealers if they were done.

add.title: Inspect or upgrade the doohickey
add.instructions: Check the balancer chain idler lever (the 'doohickey') and its spring. Many owners replace it with an aftermarket kit while the left cover is off.
add.reason: The stock part is the KLR's best-known weak spot, and owners still replace it on newer bikes.

add.title: Check the harness where it meets the frame
add.instructions: Follow the main harness along the frame and look for chafed insulation, especially on 2008-2009 bikes.
add.reason: The 09V062 recall fixed a harness that rubbed through and cut engine power.

recalls.fix: Dealer strips paint from the tabs and fits new bolts free.

recalls.what: Main wiring harness can chafe on the frame and cut engine power.

recalls.fix: Dealer replaces all four turn signals free.

known.title: The doohickey
known.what: The balancer chain idler lever and spring can fail.
